description: Vector is the historical Anki companion robot addressed by the official Vector SDK Alpha. The SDK exposes camera, proximity/touch sensing, facial recognition/enrollment, expressive animation and text-to-speech. Its documented setup has Vector and the computer on the same network while the companion app is disconnected; this differs from Cozmo’s phone-app/USB SDK path. The behavior API describes attempting to locate a visual charger marker for docking and provides a motorized lift with software height limits of 32–92 mm. Those API limits are not body dimensions, payload or guaranteed docking performance. These records do not establish Vector 2.0 specifications, current voice/cloud service, app compatibility, a current sale price or present delivery.

description: LOVOT is Groove X's slow-relation companion robot, positioned as a home robot that responds to touch, voice and its surroundings rather than performing household tasks. The manufacturer describes a sensor horn with a hemispherical camera and microphone, illumination and thermal cameras, deep-learning decision making, six-layer eye displays with more than one billion combinations, a synthesized voice, a body covered in touch sensors, autonomous movement and return-to-nest charging. The reviewed pages compare LOVOT 3.0 and 2.0 hardware: OLED versus LCD eyes, different camera sets, compute and storage, and approximately 4.6 kg versus 4.3 kg body mass. Groove X reports more than 20,000 active contracts as of July 2026 and use in homes and more than 1,200 companies. The pages describe pilot deployments and a Shiseido joint study; they do not establish independent therapeutic efficacy or a safety certification.

Mobile home companion unveiled September 4, 2026 for independently living seniors. Tuya describes LiDAR navigation, voice interaction, reminders and smart-home coordination. Commercial availability and price were not announced.

Desktop telepresence robot. An August 31 announcement planned crowdfunding for September 15; a September 14 update postponed it to September 18, 2026. Product launch remains planned for October; crowdfunding had not started at the September 16 research cutoff.

Palm-sized plush AI emotional companion with circular eye displays, powered by Huawei's Xiaoyi large model; reacts to voice, touch and shaking and keeps an interaction diary. Launched in China alongside the Mate 80 series and sold out at launch.

Egg-shaped, palm-sized AI pocket pet (a physical Tamagotchi successor) that grows through egg, baby, teen and adult stages based on interaction XP, with long-term voice and activity memory. Unveiled at CES 2026 and crowdfunded on Kickstarter. Takway AI was founded in Shenzhen in 2024.

Lifelike robotic cat for older adults and people with dementia. It responds to touch and motion with VibraPurr purring, meows and movement, comes in orange tabby, silver and tuxedo, and runs on 4 C batteries.

navel is a social robot from Munich for nursing homes. It uses LLM-based conversation in 74 languages, recognizes faces and emotions, remembers past conversations and has expressive 3D-lens eyes. It runs on an NVIDIA Jetson AGX Xavier with lidar, sonar and depth sensing. A pre-series pilot has run in German care homes since October 2023.

AI pet robot sold in two characters (Noa and Niko). Its on-device AI reacts to the owner's sleep patterns, mood and presence and keeps working offline. It moves around the home to greet people at the door, dances to music and responds to gestures. Optional care plans are sold separately.

Licensed Transformers Grimlock robot that converts itself between dinosaur and robot modes. It has 34 servos, recognises 42 voice commands and plays more than 150 original G1 audio lines. It can be controlled and programmed from an app over Bluetooth.

Licensed Transformers Megatron robot that converts itself between tank and robot forms. It has 36 servos and 112 LEDs, more than 270 voice lines and over 50 voice commands. It offers five programming modes (block, voice, manual, easy and PC). Made with Hasbro.

Licensed Transformers G1 Soundwave robot that converts itself into a cassette-player form and doubles as a Bluetooth speaker. It has 28 servos, 48 voice commands and more than 200 lines recorded by the original voice actor. The app offers joystick control and free programming.

ECOVACS' first emotional AI companion robot (FAMIBOT line), shaped like a small plush dog. It recognises faces, gestures and voices and has five personality types and seven core emotions. Its expressive eyes and articulated head react to touch, and it can mimic voices. The camera switches off in sleep mode and images are stored on the device. Shown at CES 2026 and launched in May 2026.

Desktop robotic terminal whose display moves on its own: it follows the user and switches between landscape and portrait. It is controlled by voice and gesture and works with AI agents to complete tasks. The Kickstarter campaign launched September 22, 2026.

Loona DeskMate is an AI desktop companion robot from KEYi Tech that uses a docked iPhone as its animated face and moves it with a 3-DoF (yaw, pitch, roll) system driven entirely by brushless servo motors. It connects to tools such as Gmail, Outlook, Slack and Notion to sort tasks and reminders, and its base provides 165 W GaN power delivery and 15 W Qi2 wireless charging. It was unveiled at CES 2026 and is sold through KEYi's online store.

Care U (Keyou) is a desktop AI companion robot launched in April 2026 by SenseAuto, SenseTime's smart-vehicle unit, as a home version of its 'New Member' cockpit emotion engine. It has a dual-microphone array with 180-degree pickup and up to 50 voiceprint IDs, a 2 MP camera, a 100 Hz six-axis gyroscope and a 1.75-inch OLED screen that rotates through 360 degrees, and it syncs a shared family memory with in-car AI, phones and PCs.

QwenNote Eva is a screenless desktop robot from Alibaba's Qwen Office (QwenWork) unit, launched at the 2026 Apsara Conference, that works with Android, iOS and HarmonyOS phones. It uses Qwen Office and DingTalk to execute tasks, take AI meeting notes and manage schedules, has a 3-axis motorized gimbal (about ±180° beam rotation, +15° pitch, ±20° horizontal) with magnetic wireless charging, and delivers up to 65 W GaN wired charging.

HAMOMO is an AI companion robot for Huawei's HarmonyOS smart cockpit, unveiled at the Huawei Qiankun technology conference in April 2026. It attaches magnetically to the top edge of a car's center display, turns its head and shows expressions in real time together with Huawei's Xiaoyi assistant, and can be detached and carried as a standalone AI companion.

iMoochi is a plush AI pet robot from ZTE's terminal business, sold in China under the nubia brand, unveiled at MWC 2026 and released in July 2026. It has five touch-sensing points, voiceprint recognition and two small eye screens, reacts by shaking its head, wagging its tail and making non-verbal sounds, supports Wi-Fi and 4G, and offers 8-10 hours of use per charge on a contact charging base.

metaDog is a bionic robotic pet dog from Elephant Robotics, sold in Husky and Shiba Inu styles as a companion pet. Like the company's metaCat, it mimics the look, fur texture and sounds of a real animal; an AI version that understands spoken language was presented at CES 2025. Elephant's online shop listed it at USD 189 in November 2026; regional prices, taxes and bundles differ.

The Haiwa Companion Robot is an elder-care companion robot in Haier's Haiwa family of household service robots, officially unveiled at AWE 2026 in Shanghai (March 2026) alongside the Haiwa Household Robot and Haiwa Cleaning Robot. It targets older family members with fall detection that triggers an app alert, scheduled reminders for dozens of medications, and health advice generated from a large health model using long-term blood-pressure records.

model: Fallen Leader Optimus Prime G1 Flagship
description: Fallen Leader Optimus Prime is a 40th-anniversary, battle-worn Flagship-grade auto-converting Transformers robot from Robosen with 27 servos and app-controlled programming modes. It is limited to 1,000 units in North America, with shipping estimated to begin in December 2026.

Robosen's Toy Story Buzz Lightyear is a Disney-licensed walking robot with 23 smart joints, movable eyes and mouth, 34 voice commands and app and web programming. A 30th-anniversary collector's edition is limited to 1,000 units in North America.

The Letianpai Desktop Robot (Chinese: 乐天派桌面机器人) is an Android-based desktop AI emotional companion robot with a large-language-model voice assistant, a 2.1-inch round touchscreen face, a 5 MP camera, 18 sensors and six micro servos for walking on a desk. It supports wireless and wired charging, automatic recharging and Android and Linux programming.

StackChan is an open-source AI desktop robot co-created by M5Stack and its community, using a CoreS3 (ESP32-S3) controller with a 2-inch touch display, camera, microphones and a body with two feedback servos for pan and tilt. Its firmware includes an AI agent, expressive animations and remote control, and it can be programmed with Arduino, UiFlow2 and ESP-IDF.

Mabu is a tabletop personal healthcare companion robot from San Francisco-based Catalia Health that holds AI-driven daily check-in conversations with patients managing chronic illness. Introduced in 2015, it has 6 degrees of freedom for head and eye movement, tracks and makes eye contact with the user, and runs on an Android tablet interface.

Keepon is a small yellow social robot created in 2003 by researchers Hideki Kozima and Marek Michalowski (BeatBots) for autism research, with cameras in its eyes and teleoperated or autonomous modes. It pans, tilts, leans and bounces to music, and in 2011 a consumer toy version, My Keepon, was released with toy maker Wow! Stuff.

Pleo is a robotic baby Camarasaurus dinosaur pet created by Furby co-inventor Caleb Chung at Ugobe of Emeryville, California, which shipped in late 2007 at 349 USD. It has 14 motors, a color camera, microphones, touch and foot sensors, and its Life OS lets its behavior develop over time; Innvo Labs later released Pleo rb (Reborn) in 2011.

Furhat is a conversational social robot head from Stockholm-based Furhat Robotics, a KTH spin-off; the current version was introduced in 2018. A projector back-lights an exchangeable animated face, and a 3-DoF motorized neck, camera-based face tracking, stereo microphones and an SDK support multi-party conversations for research, education and customer service.

Welli is UBTECH's mobile companion robot for seniors in care facilities, launched in August 2022. It recognizes residents by face, proactively engages them in conversation and cognitive training, gives schedule and medication reminders, enables video calls with family and remote monitoring, and navigates with a 270-degree lidar; it has a 10.1-inch main screen plus a 5.5-inch expression screen.

metaPanda is a touch-responsive robotic panda companion from Elephant Robotics that performs stretching movements when touched. An AI version with language understanding was presented alongside metaCat AI and metaDog AI at CES 2025. Elephant's online shop listed it at USD 349 in November 2026; regional prices, taxes and bundles differ.

Pubbo is an AI companion robot for children aged 3 to 11 from Shanghai-based WhalesBot, combining conversational AI, a 5 MP camera for visual recognition, a 3.5-inch touchscreen, multi-zone touch sensing and dual microphones. Children can drive it on silicone wheels across an included 800 x 800 mm map and design its movements with visual coding; it has a 5,200 mAh battery rated for 2+ hours and launched in the US in November 2026.

MoYa is a camera-free sleep-soothing robot from SoulX (Shenzhen Honghuo Intelligent Technology) that simulates hugging and rhythmic patting with a self-developed soft pneumatic structure driven by an air pump instead of electric motors. Sensors follow the user's breathing so the patting rhythm and force adapt dynamically; SoulX plans to launch it first in North America in 2026.

FR-NIA is an 11-inch (28 cm) desktop companion robot from Shanghai-based Figurobot with a biomimetic face covered in 2 mm silicone skin. Ten degrees of freedom across the face and neck drive coordinated eye, eyebrow and mouth movements with 0.01° control accuracy, while multimodal perception tracks user position and sound direction. It launched on Kickstarter in October 2026 in Lite, Pro and Pro Max configurations with early-bird pricing from 599 USD.

Flagship Bumblebee is Robosen's officially licensed auto-converting Transformers G1 Bumblebee that transforms between a walking robot and a Volkswagen Beetle with front-wheel steering and a custom hub servo. It has 31 servo-driven smart joints, 67 microchips and a six-axis motion sensor, responds to voice commands, and can be programmed manually, with blocks, on PC via Robosen Studio or by voice.

Bumblebee G1 Performance is a non-transforming programmable Transformers Bumblebee robot from Robosen driven by 17 servo motors. It responds to 20 voice commands, plays 69 original G1 animation sound clips, supports manual and block-based programming of its body parts, and runs on a 1,460 mAh lithium-ion battery.

The WALL-E Collector's Set (WALL-E and EVE) belongs to Robosen's MINI Robots line of Disney and Pixar figures, which use a cartridge-style base integrating servo motors, circuit boards, battery, speaker and connectivity. The base offers a playback mode for built-in actions and sounds and a programming mode for custom actions via Robosen Studio; the line opened for pre-order in September 2025 alongside Toy Story sets and kits.

Home companion robot series from Hisense, shown at AWE 2026 and launched in July 2026 for elderly care and family use. It offers emotional companionship, learning games for children, reminders and elderly monitoring including fall detection, and voice control of whole-home Hisense appliances.

Zoomer Dino ("Boomer") is a robotic baby Tyrannosaurus rex toy from Toronto-based Spin Master, the maker of the Zoomer robot dog, unveiled in 2014. It reacts to touch, gestures and voice commands, can be taught tricks such as sitting and was announced at around 100 USD; it was later named a Toy Industry Association Toy of the Year and followed by Zoomer Kitty.

Amoo is a small bipedal home companion robot from Shanghai-based Cyan Robotics, presented at AWE 2026 as an embodied character robot with a plush, fully soft-covered dragon-like body under 80 cm tall. It uses the company's Agentic OS and emotion-gait model for expressive eye, voice and body responses, has whole-body touch sensing and automatic recharging, and was shown ahead of its market launch.

Xiao Nuo (formerly Hobbs 3) is a lifelike half-body bionic robot from Beijing-based Noetix Robotics, launched in May 2025, consisting of a realistic female head, neck and chest unit for companionship, reception, live streaming and education. Its head has 32 active and 8 passive degrees of freedom driven by cables and linkages to reproduce human micro-expressions and lip-sync, with platinum silicone skin, two eye cameras, a chest touchscreen and camera, a microphone array and LLM-based conversation; the unit measures 400 x 300 x 600 mm and weighs 10.5 kg.

Mushroom-shaped, battery-powered desk companion robot (model ARTIFACT-01) that turns its glowing head toward activity, recognizes familiar people with an onboard camera, microphones and on-device AI, and plays nature-inspired light and sound experiences instead of acting as a voice assistant. Offered from late 2026 at a 649 USD First Access price against an 849 USD reference price.

Robotic golden retriever puppy for older adults that wags, snuggles and simulates a heartbeat when touched and uses BarkBack technology to bark in response to speech; runs on four C batteries. First introduced by Hasbro in 2016 and now sold by Hasbro spin-off Ageless Innovation.

KOMPAI-4, marketed as KOMPAI Assist, is an autonomous assistive robot from French company Kompai Robotics designed for nursing homes and elder-care facilities. It patrols premises to detect falls, offers a guided walking-bar accessory for mobility exercises, and runs entertainment and cognitive-stimulation activities for residents.

KOMPAI Cat is an emotional-support robotic companion made by French company Kompai Robotics, built as a realistic plush cat with hidden sensors that react to touch with purring and movement. It is used in elder-care and assisted-living settings as a non-drug therapeutic aid to reduce isolation and encourage interaction in residents with cognitive impairment.

Tessa is a tabletop social care robot made by Dutch company Tinybots (now operating as Tessa.Care) for people with dementia or other cognitive impairments. Caregivers and family configure it through a companion app to proactively remind users about routines such as eating, hydration and medication, and Dutch home-care organizations report it reduces the number of in-person care visits needed per day.

RoBoHoN is a small humanoid "robot phone" from Sharp that can walk, dance, sing, hold conversations, learn family members' faces, and make calls on its LTE model, sold with a monthly Cocoro service subscription. It launched in 2016 and marked its 10th anniversary with an owners' event in 2026, remaining in sale with Wi-Fi (145,200 JPY) and LTE (239,800 JPY) variants.

Amagami Ham Ham ("gentle biting Ham Ham") is a soft plush companion robot from Yukai Engineering that gently nibbles on a user's fingertip using a "Hamgorithm" that randomly cycles through about 24 different biting patterns, meant to feel like a pet or baby's affectionate bite. It launched at CES 2022 in Yuzu (cat) and Kotaro (Shiba Inu) character designs based on Liv Heart's Nemu Nemu plush line, later adding licensed designs such as Disney's Chip 'n Dale and the Gintama anime.

Topa is an animatronic entertainment robot unveiled by Sber's Robotics Center at the AI Journey 2024 conference, developed with Russian animation studio Soyuzmultfilm and inspired by Russian fairy-tale characters. It has taken its first steps and speaks with a neural-network-generated voice; Sber says it will eventually be able to run and dance to entertain children. It was presented as part of a four-robot family alongside Kuba, Krab and Slon.

My Real Baby was an animatronic robotic baby doll marketed by iRobot from 2000 in partnership with Hasbro, built around an emotionally expressive and responsive robot platform iRobot called 'IT'. It used animatronic facial expressions to simulate an infant's moods and reactions.

My Special Aflac Duck is a social robot made by Sproutel for children with cancer or sickle cell disease, helping them prepare for medical procedures and communicate feelings through soft interactive play. A clinical trial of 160 patients ages 3-10 across 8 US hospitals found it reduced distress, pain and nausea during inpatient visits compared with standard care.

Jerry the Bear was a robotic teddy bear from Sproutel built on an Android platform with 19 sensors sewn into its fur, letting a child with type 1 diabetes check its glucose level, feed it, give it insulin injections and otherwise rehearse real diabetes-care scenarios through play. First production bears shipped in 2014 via crowdfunding. Sproutel has since rebranded as Empath Labs, and 'Jerry the Bear' no longer appears among its current products; Empath Labs' current type-1-diabetes companion is marketed as Breakthrough T1D's licensed 'Rufus, the Bear with Diabetes.'

Purrble Companion is an interactive plush robot developed by Sproutel with Committee for Children whose simulated heartbeat quickens to show distress; holding and petting it slows the heartbeat into a calming purr, helping children self-regulate strong emotions. It was listed as sold out on the brand's official site as of late 2026.

Dinsaw Mini Elderly Care is a home companion robot from Thailand's CT Asia Robotics that keeps older adults company and links them to caregivers and a 24-hour monitoring centre. It answers video calls, plays music and prayer content, gives medication and health-routine reminders, lets users call a caregiver by button, touchscreen or voice, and alerts staff if a person leaves their bed; CT Asia Robotics began exporting the elderly-care robot to Japan in 2016.

Gatebox is a cylindrical character-display appliance made by Gatebox Inc. of Tokyo that projects an interactive 3D holographic AI character onto the inside of an enclosed glass tube, letting a user talk to it via a built-in human-presence sensor, microphone and speaker. The mass-production GTBX-100 model shipped in Japan in October 2019, following a 300-unit limited first-generation GTBX-1 sold in 2016.

iPal, marketed in China as the i-Bao robot (i宝机器人), is a 1.05 m tall humanoid companion robot built by AvatarMind for child companionship/education and elder-care monitoring, running on Android with vision-, voice- and touch-based interaction and an open developer interface for schools and care facilities. First shown around 2017 for kids and the elderly, AvatarMind now sells it as part of a broader AI elder-care and smart-kindergarten product line in China.

Furby (2023) is Hasbro's fifth-generation re-release of its interactive plush robot toy, announced June 22, 2023, with five voice-activated modes and over 600 responses to petting, shaking and feeding. Unlike the earlier Furby Connect, it has no app or Bluetooth connectivity and uses drawn (non-LCD) eyes, and it understands commands in eleven languages including English, Spanish, French, German and Japanese.

Project Luna is a desktop AI companion robot concept Samsung unveiled at its 'Design Is an Act of Love' exhibition during Milan Design Week 2026 (April 20-26, 2026). It takes the form of a small round-faced unit with a rotating circular display on top that reacts with voice and motion, shown as the device that welcomes and later says goodbye to exhibition visitors while illustrating Samsung's AI vision of connecting home appliances.

Eiliko is a palm-sized wearable AI companion made by Energize Lab (maker of the Eilik desktop robot) that clips onto clothing or bags like an accessory. It has a small full-color face screen that shows moods and animations, responds to tapping, petting and shaking, and can chat via an online AI connection; each unit pairs permanently to one owner the first time it is activated.

CocoMate is a small egg-shaped, clip-on AI companion toy from Haivivi, the maker of the BubblePal talking toy. It has a touch-sensitive glowing top panel, a built-in speaker and a carry strap, and Haivivi markets it as the first AI toy built on an end-to-end voice model for live spoken conversation.

PingPal is an AI interactive companion toy from Haivivi, maker of the BubblePal talking toy, marketed as 'PingPal - World's 1st Multi-Content AI Interactive Kids Toy' with a screen-free, Montessori-aligned design. As of November 2026 it is a Kickstarter pre-launch project ('Launching soon', 0 backers, no price set), linked from Haivivi's own site.

Percy is a handmade, lifelike robotic companion cat from Chongker, a Chinese maker of simulated plush-animal pets, aimed at elderly users (including people with Alzheimer's or related dementia) and children. It has five touch sensors across its body that trigger over 30 real-cat vocalizations plus a simulated purr and heartbeat when petted, voice-reactive behavior to spoken cues like 'hello Percy', paw-integrated touch controls, and a rechargeable battery rated for about 18 hours of use.

LIITE is a blind-box collectible AI plush toy sold by Haivivi (maker of BubblePal and CocoMate) under its TapDoki lifestyle art-toy line, pairing a furry designer character doll with a companion smartphone app that shows a virtual room and lets owners interact with their Doki character. Each box contains one of several randomly assigned costumed character designs, following a collect-them-all format.

Fingerlings is a 2017 WowWee toy line of small robotic creatures, originally modeled on a pygmy marmoset, that clip around a finger and react to touch and sound with built-in microphones and motion sensors, producing over 40 sounds and reactions such as blinking, singing and blowing kisses. It became the top-selling Christmas toy of 2017 in the US, UK and Canada, spawning a larger Fingerlings Hugs plush version in 2018 and later animal variants including sloths, pandas and dragons.

Hatchimals is a Spin Master toy line launched October 7, 2016, built around an egg-shaped robotic creature that physically hatches itself out of its shell after a period of interaction such as petting and talking to the egg. It launched with five animal species (Bearakeet, Burtle, Draggle, Penguala and Owlicorn) at a suggested retail price around 60 USD and became the top-selling holiday toy of 2016, before the company shifted its main line to the non-robotic Hatchimals Colleggtibles figures in 2017 and reintroduced the robotic concept as Hatchimals Alive in 2024.

Present Pets is a Spin Master interactive plush puppy toy launched for the 2020 holiday season, packaged inside a bow-topped gift box. Pulling an oversized gift tag triggers the puppy inside to bark and paw its way out of the box over about two minutes until the front panel falls open to reveal the pup. It shipped in two blind-box themes, Fancy Pups and Glitter Pups, each containing one of two possible puppy designs.

Squawkers McCaw is an animatronic blue-and-yellow macaw toy Hasbro sold under its FurReal Friends brand from 2007 to 2009, packaged with a toy cracker, remote control and perch. Six touch sensors and a microphone let it react to petting, feeding and up to eight pre-programmed spoken phrases, with recorded squawks and affirmative or hiccupping sounds depending on how it is fed and handled.

ZhuZhu Pets is a line of robotic plush hamster toys created by Cepia LLC of St. Louis, launched under the name Go Go Pets in mid-2009 and rebranded ZhuZhu Pets that October. Each hamster can be switched between a nurturing mode, where it coos and purrs when petted, and an adventure mode, where it moves on its own and reacts to obstacles and accessories in its habitat; it originally retailed for about 9 USD and became one of the best-selling toys of the 2009 holiday season.

Poo-Chi is a robot dog toy manufactured by Sega Toys and released April 1, 2000, distributed outside Japan and Korea by Hasbro's Tiger Electronics as a budget-priced alternative to Sony AIBO. It uses a light sensor in its nose and a touch sensor on its head to trigger barks, tail wags and one of six built-in songs, and it sold more than 10 million units worldwide within 8 months of launch at 24.99 USD in the US before being discontinued in 2002.

Tekno the Robotic Puppy, also sold as the Teksta Interactive Robotic Puppy, is an electronic robot dog toy developed by ToyQuest and Genesis Toys that launched in late 2000 at 39.99 USD. It offered more than 160 emotions and functions driven by motor and light sensors, could be taught voice commands, and performed tricks like fetching with a bundled bone and ball; it sold over 7 million units in its first season and more than 40 million over its first four years.

Teddy Ruxpin is an animatronic talking-bear toy launched in 1985 by Worlds of Wonder, with motor-driven eyes and mouth synced to stories played from a built-in audio cassette (later digital cartridge) deck that also carries a hidden motion-control data track. It became one of the best-selling toys of 1985 and 1986 with more than 8 million units produced, and the line has been revived by successive manufacturers (Hasbro in 1991-1996, Yes! Entertainment in 1998, BackPack Toys in 2006, and Wicked Cool Toys most recently) through 2019.

i-Cybie is a robotic dog made by Hong Kong toy company Silverlit and distributed by Tiger Electronics from January 2001 as a lower-cost rival to Sony AIBO, retailing around 200 USD versus the AIBO ERS-111's price of over 1500 USD. It has 16 motors giving 16 degrees of freedom, three onboard CPUs for motion, audio and speaker-dependent voice recognition with biometric authentication, four microphones for sound localization, and a Walk-Up Charger accessory that lets it autonomously seek out and dock with its charging station.

Petit Qoobo is a smaller, portable version of Yukai Engineering's tailed cushion robot Qoobo, sized to be carried outside the home or left resting on a desk. Like the original Qoobo, it has no face but wags a lifelike tail in response to being petted, and it adds reactions to ambient sound and voice plus a soft simulated heartbeat. It launched in Japan on December 19, 2020.

A Friend is a soft-bodied AI companion device from the Tyrol, Austria startup Beans & Bits GmbH, combining cat-ear-shaped plush ears, an illuminated pixel-eye face and voice interaction with interchangeable outer shells for different colors. Built on the open-source OpenClaw personal-AI-agent framework, it remembers what its owner tells it between conversations, supports more than 20 languages, and can set alarms, manage to-dos, assist with cooking, recommend films and handle calendar entries and messages. The company launched Indiegogo crowdfunding for it in November 2026, with working prototypes but no finished product yet and shipping targeted for Q2 2027.

FurReal My Minis are palm-sized, five-inch animatronic plush pets (a calico kitty, a brown-and-white pup and a pink piglet) released in 2024 by Just Play under license from Hasbro as part of the revived FurReal interactive-pet toy brand. Each moves its head and tail and makes animal sounds when stroked, and ships in a house-shaped display box small enough to carry in a pocket or backpack.

Omnibot 2000 is a 25-inch-tall home robot toy made by Tomy in the mid-1980s, with a built-in cassette-tape deck in its chest that could record and play back sequences of remote-controlled movements and spoken commands on a timer, plus a controllable right arm and motorized accessory tray for carrying small objects such as cups and glasses. It followed the original Omnibot and led to further variants including the voice-command Omnibot OOM (sold in North America as Hearoid) and the smaller Omnibot Jr./Robie Jr. and Verbot models.

Verbot, sold in Japan as KI*KU*ZO, is a 9-inch-tall robot toy made by Tomy in the 1980s as a smaller, cheaper companion to the Omnibot line. It is driven by a single motor and gear train that lets it move forward, backward, left and right, pick up small objects, and blink and smile to show personality, and it is voice-programmed by holding a button on its body while speaking the matching command into its wireless remote control, storing up to eight commands until it is powered off.

Primopuel is a plush-bodied talking companion doll Bandai released in Japan on November 13, 1999, co-developed with toy company Wiz. It uses seven built-in sensors and switches to react to touch and speech, singing and talking (around 280 words in the original C-type model) while its mood and personality shift based on how often and how it is handled, and it includes a clock and calendar so its conversation changes by time of day and season. It sold more than one million units in its first five years and became especially popular with middle-aged and elderly users, including use in elder-care settings, alongside children.

Familiar is the debut home-companion robot from Familiar Machines & Magic (FMM), a Boston-area startup founded by former iRobot CEO Colin Angle and co-founders Chris Jones and Ira Renfrew. Unlike a cleaning or talking robot, it is designed as an animal-like physical presence that expresses itself through body language, facial expressions and vocalizations, learns household routines, and builds a distinct personality and memory of its owner over time, storing its data on-device by default. It was unveiled in May 2026; the company has not yet disclosed a shipping date or price.

Jumper is an open-source crab-shaped robot from Beijing-based KingKong Technology, a company that originally made robot encoders and tactile servos. Its 400x400x200 mm crab-style body carries 22 high-torque tactile servos, weighs 1.8 kg, moves at over 0.5 m/s, can jump higher than 400 mm, grasp loads up to 1 kg, and runs about 2 hours per charge. The company released it as open-source hardware in 2026 with a free giveaway of 100 units.

Hiro-chan (Kamatte Hiro-chan) is a baby-shaped therapeutic companion robot from Vstone made for elder care. Covered in soft plush fabric over an internal chassis, it uses an accelerometer to react to being held, rocked or bounced and plays authentic recorded baby sounds. It runs on three AA batteries and is aimed at nursing homes, day-care centers and home caregivers, with a developer edition sold as Hiro-chan-R.

CommU is a tabletop social-dialogue robot co-developed by Vstone with Osaka University researchers Hiroshi Ishiguro and Yuichiro Yoshikawa. Its many degrees of freedom in the eyes, head and body let it direct its gaze at specific people in a group conversation and show listening behaviors, creating a sense of natural multi-party dialogue; it was unveiled alongside the companion robot Sota in January 2015.

Fufuly is a soft, cloud-shaped robotic pillow from Yukai Engineering, developed with the University of Tokyo, that simulates a breathing rhythm so the person holding it unconsciously synchronizes their own breathing (entrainment) for relaxation and stress relief. It was unveiled as a CES 2023 Innovation Award honoree and won the Chicago Good Design Award 2024.

Baby Fu-Fu is a handy fan robot from Yukai Engineering, roughly twice the size of its sibling Nekojita Fu-Fu, built to blow a gentle, adjustable three-speed breeze on babies and small children. Its hands and feet clamp onto a stroller handle to aim the airflow, and its mouth fully encloses the spinning fan so little fingers cannot reach it; it was announced in January 2026 for a summer 2026 launch.

Telenoid R1 is a minimalist teleoperated android created by Hiroshi Ishiguro's lab at ATR, designed to carry a remote operator's voice and head/body movements to the person it sits in front of so they experience talking with that person rather than a robot. Covered in soft silicone with a deliberately ambiguous, genderless appearance, it has been used for remote work meetings, language teaching and letting isolated elderly people converse with distant family; it debuted in August 2010 with a roughly $8,000 commercial unit alongside a $35,000 research version.

CutieroidDoll Frame Arms Girl Gourai is a character robot doll from HatsuMuv modeled on the Frame Arms Girl franchise's Gourai, with 11 motorized axes (3 in the head, 4 per arm) plus free-moving torso, leg and wrist joints. It reacts to voice and touch sensors, tracks sound with its face, recognizes items via RFID, and ships with 97 performance routines, about 200 voiced lines and 47 motion patterns, controllable over Bluetooth from a companion app. Pre-orders opened in November 2026 for an August 2027 release.

Kirobo Mini is a palm-sized communication-partner robot from Toyota that holds basic conversations, makes small hand gestures and responds to the facial expressions it reads through its built-in camera, pairing over Bluetooth with a companion smartphone app. It began sales at select Japanese Toyota dealers in winter 2016 ahead of a nationwide rollout in 2017.

HT-X2 is a multifunctional embodied elder-care robot from Hangzhou-based Huaxi Tech (骅羲科技), one of the first companies the maker says has brought such a robot to market for home and institutional elderly care. It incorporates the company's own dexterous-hand and robotic-arm designs and elder-care AI model, and has been deployed across more than 20 Chinese provinces and various care institutions.

Kangkang (心忆康康) is a mobile home-companion robot from Beijing-based HeartMemo (心忆科技), built by a team pairing psychology and computer-science research into emotional computing. It moves around the home to approach family members, converses naturally, sings, tells stories, proactively starts conversations at appropriate moments, and keeps a layered family memory using the company's own BSLA companionship-decision framework; it ships in ivory, brown, pink and orange, and won a GEIA Excellence Service Robot award.

Sparko is widely cited as the first known robotic pet, a robot dog built by Westinghouse Electric and shown publicly in 1940 (alongside Westinghouse's humanoid robot Elektro) performing pre-programmed tricks like sitting and barking. It was never sold commercially due to limited public interest, making it a historical showpiece rather than a consumer product.

Abi is a humanoid companion robot made by Australian startup Andromeda Robotics for aged-care and assisted-living residents, engaging them through conversation, games and social interaction tailored to individual personalities, abilities and languages. It is deployed in Australian aged-care facilities such as mecwacare and the Medical & Aged Care Group, with the company expanding its reach toward the US (including the San Francisco Bay Area) as of 2026.

Ruko 1088 Smart Robot is a 15.8-inch-tall consumer toy robot that dances to music with expressive movements and supports customizable dance routines. It is sold through Ruko's Amazon storefront in the US as part of the Hong Kong brand's holiday 2026 toy lineup.

Ruko 6088 Programmable Robot is a consumer toy robot with gesture-sensing controls, an expressive LED face, and customizable action sequences. It is sold through Ruko's Amazon storefront in the US as part of the Hong Kong brand's holiday 2026 toy lineup.

Ruko 8809 Robot Dinosaur is a consumer toy robot dinosaur with roaring sounds, dynamic walking movements, interactive remote controls and a soft foam dart-firing feature. It is sold through Ruko's Amazon storefront in the US as part of the Hong Kong brand's holiday 2026 toy lineup.

Bubbo 1 (巴布) is a home AI companion robot from Beijing-based Xinyan Robotics, built around the company's own "Xinyuan" emotional-companionship language model and "Bubbo OS" robot operating system to deliver native multimodal perception, long-term memory, emotion understanding and proactive, in-the-moment interaction. It stands about 65 cm tall with a rounded cream-and-apricot body and expressive animated eyes that react to touch and context, positioning it as a family-companionship device rather than an industrial platform.

Lyra S1 is an ultra-bionic interactive robot face/head unveiled by Hangzhou Lingyan Technology (brand FaceSoul), using a cable-driven bionic-muscle mechanism to reach 32 facial degrees of freedom, dynamic pupils with visual tracking for eye contact, and a proprietary multimodal 'Amygdala' model that generates real-time lip-synced micro-expressions from speech instead of preset animations. It is sold as an embodied-AI interaction module to humanoid-robot OEMs plus education, research and commercial-service customers, with a lower-cost consumer companion version planned later; the core team originates from Jilin University's engineering bionics lab.
